name: Mixed-video diagnostic repair 2026-10-22
document:
PURPOSE AND SCOPE

Annotate visible object instances in every registered frame of
frameset_5e6b3d08c73f4488a16e84f5396f28d5. Preserve all source identities, checksums, frame identities, timestamps and dimensions.

This is a diagnostic corpus. Its suitability must be established by
completed annotations and validation, rather than assumed from its size.

OBJECT CLASSES

Use the most specific supported COCO class that the visible pixels justify. The extended classes microphone, headphones, camera, watch and tablet are also available.

Use other only for a recognizable physical object that has no suitable
supported class. Supply a short, consistent descriptive name. Do not use other as a substitute for an uncertain supported class.

Text, code, interface controls, logos, icons, decorative graphics and
abstract diagrams are outside this object task. Record relevant exclusions in out_of_taxonomy. Do not create other boxes around them.

VISIBILITY AND BOXES

Include independently recognizable objects whose visible bounding box is at least 8 pixels wide and 8 pixels high.

Use integer source-pixel coordinates [x, y, width, height]. Draw a tight
box around the visible extent, clip it to the image boundaries, and do not infer hidden portions behind an occluder.

Annotate distinct objects separately, including objects held by people. For people, require a recognizable face or coherent head/body instance; isolated limbs do not constitute a person annotation.

Do not use neighboring frames, transcripts or model predictions to infer an object that cannot be identified in the current frame.

SUBSETS

live: an object belonging to the primary filmed scene.

screen: a recognizable photographic object depicted inside a display,
webpage, thumbnail, photograph or video within the primary scene.

composited: a recognizable photographic object deliberately overlaid
outside such a display, including a cut-out or picture-in-picture subject.

A physical monitor is a live tv object when appropriate. Independently
recognizable objects shown within its display are separate screen objects.
A filmed monitor or software interface does not automatically provide
screen-object instances.

Assign one subset to each instance. Do not change subset labels to meet coverage targets.

FRAME REVIEW AND UNCERTAINTY

Inspect every registered frame. An empty object list is valid only after
the frame has been inspected and no eligible object was found.

Code and diagram frames may legitimately be negative examples. Annotate eligible photographic objects if present; do not invent positives.

Use uncertain=true to flag an annotation needing adjudication. Record the reason through the available review notes. If identity remains unresolved after adjudication, exclude it from scored objects and retain the reason in the adjudication log.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW

Two different human reviewers must annotate independently without seeing
each other's annotations or candidate-model predictions. A third human adjudicator resolves disagreements in labels, subsets, inclusion and boxes.

Complete review of every frame and freeze the adjudicated annotations before using candidate predictions for evaluation.

ACCEPTANCE

Retain the existing diagnostic requirements:
- Exact membership of the five frozen source hashes.
- At least 50 non-person COCO instances across five non-person COCO classes.
- At least 20 live, 20 screen and 10 composited COCO instances.
- At least 15 small objects with box area below 2% of frame area.
- At least 15 large objects with box area above 20% of frame area.
- No source contributes more than 60% of all annotated COCO instances.
- Complete independent review and adjudication.

Extended classes, including other, do not satisfy COCO adequacy gates and are reported separately from COCO detector scores.

If coverage is insufficient, record the shortfall and prepare a new corpus with suitable additional sources. Do not relabel, duplicate annotations, omit registered frames or lower thresholds to obtain a pass.

REPAIR PROVENANCE — 2026-10-22

This replacement binds the existing 62-frame corpus to its exact five source digests and explicitly enables the extended taxonomy described above. Earlier completed assignments were confirmed by the coordinator to be AI/automated sessions. Preserve them as assisted annotation history; they do not establish independent human passes. A fresh template must begin blank. Do not copy assisted outputs into completed human passes, attest to independent humans, or promote a model/release on that basis. Screen examples must be photographic objects inside displays, not interfaces, icons or rendered game content. Perfume rendering eligibility must be resolved from visible evidence rather than assumed.
